cleanup.py:
"""Text cleanup: protect pasted code/data, remove conversational noise.

Pure functions, no I/O, no AI. Safe to run on every keystroke.
"""

import math
import re

__all__ = ["protect_materials", "clean_text", "estimate_tokens"]


def estimate_tokens(text):
    """Approximate token count. Code averages ~3.5-4 chars/token; we use 3.8."""
    return math.ceil(len(text or "") / 3.8)


# ==========================================================================
# Step 1 - protect code blocks and pasted data
# ==========================================================================
# Anything inside ``` ``` or """ """ is treated as material: kept word-for-word.
MATERIAL_RE = re.compile(r"(```.*?```|\"\"\".*?\"\"\")", re.DOTALL)


def protect_materials(text):
    """Replace code/data blocks with [MATERIAL n] placeholders.

    Returns (text_with_placeholders, list_of_materials).
    """
    materials = []

    def _swap(match):
        block = match.group(0)
        if block.startswith('"""'):
            block = block[3:-3].strip("\n")   # plain pasted text: drop the quotes
        materials.append(block)                # ``` blocks are kept with fences
        return f"[MATERIAL {len(materials)}]"

    return MATERIAL_RE.sub(_swap, text), materials


# ==========================================================================
# Step 2 - rule-based cleanup (no AI, instant)
# ==========================================================================
_GREETING = re.compile(
    r"^(hi|hello|hey|dear|good (morning|afternoon|evening))\b"
    r"( there| claude| chatgpt| gpt| ai| assistant| team| bro| buddy)?[\s,!.:\-]*",
    re.I,
)
_LEAD_IN = re.compile(r"^(so|okay|ok|well|alright|basically|now)[,\s]+", re.I)
_REQUEST = re.compile(
    r"^(i was wondering if|i wonder if|i would like you to|i'd like you to|"
    r"i want you to|i need you to|is it possible (for you )?to|"
    r"would it be possible (for you )?to|"
    r"(can|could|would|will) (you|u)( please| pls| plz| kindly| possibly)?|"
    r"(you|u) (can|could|would)( please| kindly)?|please( kindly)?|pls|plz|kindly)\s+",
    re.I,
)
# A whole sentence that carries no instruction -> drop it.
_EMPTY_SENTENCE = re.compile(
    r"^(thanks|thank you|thx|ty|cheers|regards|best regards|hope you can help|"
    r"i hope (this|that) makes sense|let me know if you (need|have)|"
    r"looking forward|appreciate (it|your help)|you are the best|you're the best|"
    r"(i )?hope you('re| are)( doing)? (well|good|fine)|how are you|hope all is well)\b",
    re.I,
)
# Words that add no meaning. ("just" and "very" are NOT removed on purpose:
# "just the summary" means "only the summary".)
_FILLER = re.compile(
    r"\b(basically|actually|literally|honestly|kind of|sort of|pretty much|"
    r"you know|i mean|please)\b,?\s*",
    re.I,
)
_BULLET = re.compile(r"^(\s*(?:[-*•]|\d+[.)])\s+)")
_SENTENCE_SPLIT = re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+")


def _clean_sentence(sentence):
    """Clean one sentence. Returns '' if the sentence should be dropped."""
    s = sentence.strip()
    if _EMPTY_SENTENCE.match(s) and len(s) < 60:
        return ""

    was_request = False
    for _ in range(4):                       # strip stacked prefixes
        before = s
        s = _GREETING.sub("", s)
        s = _LEAD_IN.sub("", s)
        new = _REQUEST.sub("", s)
        if new != s:
            was_request = True
        s = new
        if s == before:
            break

    if _EMPTY_SENTENCE.match(s) and len(s) < 60:   # e.g. "Hi, hope you're well!"
        return ""
    s = _FILLER.sub("", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\s{2,}", " ", s).strip(" ,")
    if not s:
        return ""
    # "Could you write X?" -> "Write X."
    if was_request and s.endswith("?"):
        s = s[:-1].rstrip() + "."
    return s[0].upper() + s[1:]


def clean_text(text):
    """Rule-based cleanup that keeps line/bullet structure."""
    text = re.sub(r"([!?.])\1+", r"\1", text)          # "!!!" -> "!"
    text = re.sub(r"[ \t]+", " ", text)
    seen = set()
    out_lines = []

    for line in text.splitlines():
        if not line.strip():
            if out_lines and out_lines[-1] != "":
                out_lines.append("")
            continue
        bullet = ""
        m = _BULLET.match(line)
        if m:
            bullet = m.group(1).strip() + " "
            line = line[m.end():]

        kept = []
        for sent in _SENTENCE_SPLIT.split(line.strip()):
            cleaned = _clean_sentence(sent)
            if not cleaned:
                continue
            key = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9 ]", "", cleaned.lower()).strip()
            if len(key.split()) > 3 and key in seen:   # repeated sentence
                continue
            seen.add(key)
            kept.append(cleaned)
        if kept:
            out_lines.append(bullet + " ".join(kept))

    return "\n".join(out_lines).strip()

def platform_pack(pid):
    return PLATFORMS.get(pid, GENERIC_PLATFORM)


def fill(template, pid, answers=None):
    """Fill {placeholders} from the platform pack, specialised by answers (e.g. SwiftUI vs UIKit)."""
    pack = dict(platform_pack(pid))
    ui = ((answers or {}).get("ui_framework") or "").lower()
    if ui and ui in pack.get("list_ui_by", {}):
        pack["list_ui"] = pack["list_ui_by"][ui]
    return re.sub(r"\{(\w+)\}", lambda m: str(pack.get(m.group(1)) or GENERIC_PLATFORM.get(m.group(1), "")), template)

CONSTRAINT = re.compile(r"\b(only|must not|don'?t|do not|without|no more than|at most|limit(?:ed)? to|never use|"
                        r"must use|no (?:external|third[- ]party|new) (?:libraries|dependencies))\b", re.I)
METRIC = re.compile(r"\b(?:under|below|less than|at most|at least|within|target(?:ing)?|<|>)\s*~?\d+(?:\.\d+)?\s*"
                    r"(?:ms|s|sec|seconds?|minutes?|fps|%|mb|gb|items?|rows?|users?|requests?)\b", re.I)
COMMA_SPLICE = re.compile(r"\b\w+,\s*(?:it|this|that|they|i|we|he|she)\s+(?!and\b|or\b|but\b)\w+", re.I)
NO_SPACE = re.compile(r"[a-z][,;](?=[a-z])", re.I)


def anatomy(clean, materials, und, intents, code_change):
    """Which parts of a strong prompt are present, filled in by the compiler, or missing."""
    def item(key, label, status, detail, evidence=""):
        return {"key": key, "label": label, "status": status, "detail": detail, "evidence": evidence}
    coding = und["coding"]
    a = [item("goal", "Goal", "present", f"{len(und['objectives'])} objective(s) found",
              und["objectives"][0]["source"][:60] if und["objectives"] else "")]
    if und["platform"] or und["signals"]["stack"]:
        ev = und["signals"]["evidence"].get(und["platform"], "") or (und["signals"]["stack"] or [{"name": ""}])[0]["name"]
        a.append(item("context", "Context", "present", "platform / stack stated", ev))
    else:
        a.append(item("context", "Context", "missing" if coding else "optional",
                      "no platform or stack" if coding else "not needed for this request"))
    if materials:
        a.append(item("inputs", "Inputs", "present", f"{len(materials)} pasted block(s)"))
    elif code_change or intents & {"review", "fix"}:
        a.append(item("inputs", "Inputs", "missing", "the code or error this is about isn't included"))
    else:
        a.append(item("inputs", "Inputs", "optional", "not required for this kind of ask"))
    m = CONSTRAINT.search(clean)
    a.append(item("constraints", "Constraints", "present" if m else ("auto" if coding else "optional"),
                  "you stated limits" if m else ("rules are added from what was detected" if coding else "none stated"),
                  m.group(0) if m else ""))
    m = EXPECT.search(clean) or METRIC.search(clean)
    if m:
        a.append(item("success", "Success criteria", "present", "expected result or a number given", m.group(0)))
    elif code_change:
        a.append(item("success", "Success criteria", "missing", "nothing says what 'done' looks like"))
    else:
        a.append(item("success", "Success criteria", "auto", "an answer shape is set per objective"))
    m = OUTPUT_FMT.search(clean)
    a.append(item("format", "Output format", "present" if m else "auto",
                  "you asked for a format" if m else "set by the compiler", m.group(0) if m else ""))
    m = EXAMPLES.search(clean)
    a.append(item("examples", "Examples", "present" if m else "optional",
                  "example or pasted material included" if m else "none (fine for most asks)", m.group(0) if m else ""))
    m = AUDIENCE.search(clean)
    if "write" in intents:
        a.append(item("audience", "Audience & tone", "present" if m else "missing",
                      "stated" if m else "who is this for, and in what tone?", m.group(0) if m else ""))
    else:
        a.append(item("audience", "Role", "auto", "set from platform and concerns"))
    return a


def readability(raw, clean):
    sentences = [x for x in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n+", clean) if x.strip()]
    lengths = [len(x.split()) for x in sentences] or [0]
    return {"sentences": len(sentences), "words": sum(lengths), "avg_words": round(sum(lengths) / len(lengths), 1),
            "longest": max(lengths), "comma_splices": [m.group(0) for m in COMMA_SPLICE.finditer(raw)][:3],
            "missing_spaces": [m.group(0) for m in NO_SPACE.finditer(raw)][:3]}


def _f(fid, dim, sev, title, why, fix="", example="", evidence="", question=None):
    return {"id": fid, "dimension": dim, "severity": sev, "title": title, "why": why, "fix": fix,
            "example": example, "evidence": evidence, "question": question}


def analyze(raw, clean, materials, und, changes, target="chat"):
    """raw: the prompt exactly as typed (for evidence); clean: normalized text; und: understand() result."""
    F = []
    intents = {o["intent"] for o in und["objectives"]}
    code_change = bool(intents & CODE_CHANGE)
    coding = und["coding"]
    mats = "\n".join(materials)
    plat = platform_pack(und["platform"])

    # ---------------- clarity ----------------
    removed = [c for c in changes if c["kind"] in ("profanity", "emotion", "intensifier")]
    if removed:
        F.append(_f("CL100", "clarity", "info", "Removed words that carry no technical meaning",
                    "Swearing, venting and intensifiers don't change what Claude should do; they only add noise.",
                    "Removed automatically.", evidence="|".join(c["from"] for c in removed)))
    seen, taken = set(), []
    for rx, why, example in _VAGUE:
        for m in rx.finditer(clean):
            word = m.group(1).lower()
            if word in seen or any(a < m.end() and m.start() < b for a, b in taken):
                continue
            # sizes / speed are handled by the knowledge-pack questions when present
            if word in ("large", "huge", "big", "massive", "many", "lots of", "a lot of") and \
                    any(q["id"] == "data_size" for q in und["questions"]):
                continue
            seen.add(word)
            taken.append((m.start(), m.end()))
            F.append(_f("CL101", "clarity", "warn", f"Vague: '{m.group(1)}'", why,
                        f"Replace '{m.group(1)}' with something checkable.", example, evidence=m.group(1)))
    m = DANGLING.search(clean)
    if m:
        F.append(_f("CL102", "clarity", "error", "Refers to a conversation Claude can't see",
                    "A new chat has no memory. Claude will guess what you're referring to.",
                    "Paste or describe it.", evidence=m.group(0)))
    rd = readability(raw, clean)
    if rd["comma_splices"]:
        F.append(_f("CL104", "clarity", "info", "Two thoughts joined by a comma",
                    "A comma splice makes the subject of the second part ambiguous ('it' = the app? the list?).",
                    "Split it into two sentences or name the subject.", "My iOS app hangs after 3 minutes.",
                    evidence=rd["comma_splices"][0]))
    if rd["longest"] > 40:
        F.append(_f("CL105", "clarity", "info", f"Very long sentence ({rd['longest']} words)",
                    "Long sentences hide separate requirements inside each other.",
                    "Split it into one requirement per sentence."))
    if len(und["objectives"]) >= 4:
        F.append(_f("CL103", "clarity", "warn", f"{len(und['objectives'])} separate asks in one prompt",
                    "Quality drops when many unrelated asks are bundled. They're numbered below, but consider "
                    "splitting the least related ones into a separate prompt."))

    # ---------------- context ----------------
    if coding:
        if not und["platform"] and not und["signals"]["stack"]:
            F.append(_f("CX200", "context", "error", "Platform / language not stated",
                        "Claude will pick a language and framework for you.",
                        "Name the platform and language.", "iOS 17 app in Swift 5.10 (SwiftUI)"))
        elif not VERSION.search(clean + "\n" + mats):
            ev = und["signals"]["evidence"].get(und["platform"], "") or \
                (und["signals"]["stack"][0]["name"] if und["signals"]["stack"] else "")
            F.append(_f("CX201", "context", "warn", "No versions",
                        "APIs differ between versions; Claude may use one your project doesn't have.",
                        "Add versions.", plat["version_example"], evidence=ev))
    refs = sorted({m.group(0) for m in REFERENCE.finditer(NEGATIVE_CLAUSE.sub("", clean))})
    if refs and not materials:
        diag = intents & {"diagnose"} and not code_change
        if target == "claude-code":
            F.append(_f("CX202", "context", "warn", "Code mentioned without a file path",
                        "Claude Code will have to search and may open the wrong file.",
                        "Add the file path.", "Sources/Features/ItemList/ItemListViewModel.swift",
                        evidence=refs[0]))
        elif code_change or intents & {"review", "explain"}:
            F.append(_f("CX202", "context", "error", "Code mentioned but not included",
                        "Claude will invent what it looks like and write code that doesn't fit yours.",
                        "Paste it inside ``` ```.", evidence=refs[0]))
        elif diag:
            F.append(_f("CX203", "context", "warn", "No code included",
                        "Without code Claude can only rank generic causes, not point at your bug.",
                        "Paste the screen / view model where the problem happens (inside ``` ```).",
                        evidence=refs[0]))
    elif "diagnose" in intents and not materials and target != "claude-code":
        F.append(_f("CX203", "context", "info", "No code included",
                    "Claude will answer with likely causes and how to confirm them, not a fix for your exact code.",
                    "Paste the relevant screen / view model inside ``` ``` for a precise fix."))

    # ---------------- specificity (knowledge-pack questions) ----------------
    for q in und["open_questions"]:
        F.append(_f("SP:" + q["id"], "specificity", q.get("severity", "warn"), f"Missing: {q['label']}", q["why"],
                    q["q"], ", ".join(q["options"][:3]), evidence=q.get("evidence", ""), question=q["id"]))

    # ---------------- verifiability ----------------
    if "fix" in intents:
        if not ERROR_TEXT.search(clean + "\n" + mats):
            F.append(_f("VR400", "verifiability", "error", "No exact error output",
                        "A description of an error makes Claude fix a guessed problem.",
                        "Paste the exact error / stack trace inside ``` ```."))
        if not (EXPECT.search(clean) and ACTUAL.search(clean)):
            F.append(_f("VR401", "verifiability", "warn", "Expected vs actual not both stated",
                        "Without both, 'fixed' has no definition.", "Add both.",
                        "Expected: second login succeeds. Actual: HTTP 500."))
    if code_change and not EXPECT.search(clean) and "fix" not in intents:
        F.append(_f("VR402", "verifiability", "error" if "build" in intents else "warn", "No definition of done",
                    "Claude will decide by itself what 'working' means.",
                    "State the expected result.", "Given a cart total of 100 and a 10% coupon, then the total is 90."))
    if code_change and not SCOPE.search(clean) and target == "claude-code":
        F.append(_f("VR403", "verifiability", "warn", "Scope not defined",
                    "Claude Code may edit files you didn't intend to touch.",
                    "Say what may change and what must not.", "Only change ItemListViewModel.swift."))
    if "tests" in intents:
        if not TEST_FRAMEWORK.search(clean + "\n" + mats):
            F.append(_f("VR404", "verifiability", "error", "Test framework not stated",
                        "Claude will choose a framework that may not match your project.",
                        "Name it.", "TestNG 7.10 + Selenium 4.21"))
    if "migrate" in intents and not MIGRATION_VERSIONS.search(clean):
        F.append(_f("VR405", "verifiability", "error", "Source and target versions missing",
                    "Breaking changes depend on the exact versions.", "Add both.", "from Swift 5.9 to Swift 6.0"))
    size = estimate_tokens(clean + mats)
    if size > 12000:
        F.append(_f("CX204", "context", "info", "Very large prompt", f"About {size} tokens.",
                    "Keep only the code that matters for this task."))

    # ---------------- scores ----------------
    order = {"error": 0, "warn": 1, "info": 2}
    F.sort(key=lambda f: (order[f["severity"]], DIMENSIONS.index(f["dimension"]), f["id"]))
    dims = {}
    for d in DIMENSIONS:
        keep = 1.0
        for f in F:
            if f["dimension"] == d:
                keep *= 1 - PENALTY[f["severity"]]
        dims[d] = round(100 * keep)
    score = round(sum(dims.values()) / len(dims))
    counts = {s: sum(1 for f in F if f["severity"] == s) for s in PENALTY}

    # ---------------- decisions Claude would otherwise make on its own ----------------
    decisions = []
    for q in und["questions"]:
        decisions.append({"what": q["label"], "kind": "missing detail", "handled": "default" if q.get("default")
                          else "ask", "objective": q.get("objective", 0)})
    for f in F:
        if f["id"] == "CL101":
            decisions.append({"what": f"meaning of '{f['evidence']}'", "kind": "vague word", "handled": "flagged",
                              "objective": 0})
    ana = anatomy(clean, materials, und, intents, code_change)
    for item in ana:
        if item["status"] == "missing":
            decisions.append({"what": item["label"].lower(), "kind": "missing part", "handled": "flagged",
                              "objective": 0})

    # ---------------- per objective ----------------
    per_obj = []
    for o in und["objectives"]:
        per_obj.append({"id": o["id"], "intent": o["label"], "confidence": o.get("confidence", "low"),
                        "cues": o.get("cues", []), "concerns": o["concerns"],
                        "missing": [q["label"] for q in und["questions"] if q.get("objective") == o["id"]],
                        "templated": o.get("templated", False)})
    return {"findings": F, "score": score, "dimensions": dims, "counts": counts, "anatomy": ana,
            "decisions": decisions, "readability": rd, "objectives": per_obj}


def spans(raw, findings, changes):
    """Character ranges in the raw prompt to highlight: [{start, end, severity, title}]."""
    out = []
    low = raw.lower()

    def mark(text, severity, title):
        if not text:
            return
        i = low.find(text.lower())
        while i >= 0:
            if not any(s["start"] < i + len(text) and i < s["end"] for s in out):
                out.append({"start": i, "end": i + len(text), "severity": severity, "title": title})
                return
            i = low.find(text.lower(), i + 1)

    for c in changes:
        if c["kind"] in ("profanity", "emotion", "intensifier"):
            mark(c["from"], "removed", "Removed (no technical meaning)")
    for f in findings:
        for ev in (f["evidence"] or "").split("|"):
            if f["id"] != "CL100":
                mark(ev, f["severity"], f["title"])
    return sorted(out, key=lambda s: s["start"])
normalize.py:
"""Normalize how people actually type into how a model should read.

  * profanity (incl. masked forms like f***, fu**ing, sh!t) and emotional venting -> removed
  * intensifiers that carry no technical meaning ("crazily", "insanely", "super")   -> removed
  * chat slang / dev shorthand ("kinda", "algo", "perf", "db", "u")                  -> expanded
  * number words before units ("three minutes")                                     -> digits
  * platform / tech names ("ios", "swiftui", "json")                                -> canonical casing

Returns the new text plus a list of what was removed or changed, so the UI can show it.
Run this on text whose code blocks are already protected (see cleanup.protect_materials).
"""

import re

# ---------- profanity (whole word, case-insensitive) ----------
_PROFANITY = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:"
    r"f+u+c+k+\w*|fu?c?k(?:ing|in|er|ed|s)?|f[\W_]*u[\W_]*c[\W_]*k\w*|fck\w*|fkn|fking|fcking|fuking|fukin\w*|fk|"
    r"motherf\w*|mf+|wtf|wth|ffs|omfg|stfu|"
    r"sh[i1!]t\w*|bullsh\w*|crap(?:py|s)?|damn\w*|dammit|goddam\w*|"
    r"bloody|bastard\w*|piss(?:ed|ing)?(?: off)?|freak(?:ing|in)|frick(?:ing|in)?|effing|"
    r"stupid|idiotic|retarded"
    r")\b", re.I)
# masked swearing: f***, fu**ing, s**t, F*ck, Fuck***
_MASKED = re.compile(r"\b[a-zA-Z]{1,5}[*#@$%]{2,}[a-zA-Z]*|\b[a-zA-Z]{1,3}[*#@$%!]+[a-zA-Z]+\b|(?<![*\w])\*{3,}")
_PHRASES = re.compile(
    r"(?:\b(?:fuck|f[*#@$%]+\w*|screw|damn|to hell with)\w*[*#@$%]*\s+(?:this|it|that|you)\b[,.!]*)|"
    r"\b(?:what the (?:hell|heck|f\w*)|the (?:hell|heck)|for (?:god'?s|f\w*'?s|christ'?s|heaven'?s) sake|"
    r"holy (?:cow|crap|shit)|oh my god|oh god|god knows)\b", re.I)
# whole clauses that only express feelings / urgency
_VENTING = re.compile(
    r"(?:^|(?<=[.!?,;]\s)|(?<=^))\s*(?:"
    r"i(?:'m| am) (?:so |really |completely |totally )?(?:frustrated|tired|done|annoyed|stuck|desperate|lost|"
    r"confused|going crazy|losing my mind|sick of (?:this|it))[^.!?,;]*|"
    r"(?:this|it) (?:is )?(?:driving me (?:crazy|nuts|insane)|killing me|makes me (?:crazy|mad))[^.!?,;]*|"
    r"i hate (?:this|it)[^.!?,;]*|"
    r"(?:please )?help(?: me)?(?: out)?(?: asap| urgently| quickly)?[!.]*(?=\s*(?:[.!?,;]|$))|"
    r"(?:this is )?(?:very |super |really )?urgent[!.]*|asap[!.]*|"
    r"nothing works[^.!?,;]*"
    r")\s*[,.!;]?", re.I | re.M)
_INTENSIFIERS = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:asap|urgently|right now|immediately)\b[!.]*|"
    r"\b(?:crazily|insanely|ridiculously|absurdly|terribly|horribly|awfully|totally|absolutely|seriously|"
    r"extremely|massively|hugely|incredibly|unbelievably|madly|wildly)\b\s*|"
    r"\b(?:super|crazy|mega|way too|so so)\s+(?=(?:slow|fast|laggy|high|big|long|bad|buggy|heavy|large|"
    r"weird|annoying|broken|often|much|many)\b)", re.I)

# ---------- slang / shorthand ----------
SLANG = {
    "kinda": "kind of", "sorta": "sort of", "gonna": "going to", "wanna": "want to", "gotta": "have to",
    "u": "you", "ur": "your", "pls": "", "plz": "", "thx": "", "ty": "", "tho": "though", "thru": "through",
    "coz": "because", "cuz": "because", "b/c": "because", "w/": "with", "w/o": "without",
    "idk": "I don't know", "dunno": "don't know", "smth": "something", "sth": "something",
    "algo": "algorithm", "algos": "algorithms", "func": "function", "funcs": "functions", "fn": "function",
    "perf": "performance", "db": "database", "dbs": "databases", "impl": "implementation",
    "env": "environment", "envs": "environments", "deps": "dependencies", "msg": "message", "msgs": "messages",
    "btn": "button", "btns": "buttons", "img": "image", "imgs": "images", "pic": "image", "pics": "images",
    "vars": "variables", "param": "parameter", "params": "parameters", "arg": "argument", "args": "arguments",
    "repo": "repository", "lib": "library", "libs": "libraries", "auth": "authentication",
    "prod": "production", "approx": "approximately", "info": "information",
}
_SLANG_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w/.-])(" + "|".join(re.escape(k) for k in sorted(SLANG, key=len, reverse=True))
                       + r")(?![\w/-]|\.\w)", re.I)

CANONICAL = {
    "ios": "iOS", "ipados": "iPadOS", "macos": "macOS", "android": "Android", "swiftui": "SwiftUI",
    "uikit": "UIKit", "xcode": "Xcode", "kotlin": "Kotlin", "java": "Java",
    "javascript": "JavaScript", "typescript": "TypeScript", "python": "Python", "flutter": "Flutter",
    "react native": "React Native", "nodejs": "Node.js", "node.js": "Node.js",
    "selenium": "Selenium", "appium": "Appium", "testng": "TestNG", "junit": "JUnit", "pytest": "pytest",
    "sql": "SQL", "api": "API", "apis": "APIs", "json": "JSON", "ui": "UI", "ux": "UX", "url": "URL",
    "http": "HTTP", "https": "HTTPS", "css": "CSS", "html": "HTML", "jetpack compose": "Jetpack Compose",
    "core data": "Core Data", "swiftdata": "SwiftData", "firebase": "Firebase", "graphql": "GraphQL",
    "voiceover": "VoiceOver", "talkback": "TalkBack", "wcag": "WCAG", "github": "GitHub",
}
_CANON_RE = re.compile(r"\b(" + "|".join(re.escape(k) for k in sorted(CANONICAL, key=len, reverse=True)) + r")\b",
                       re.I)

_NUM = {"one": 1, "two": 2, "three": 3, "four": 4, "five": 5, "six": 6, "seven": 7, "eight": 8, "nine": 9,
        "ten": 10, "eleven": 11, "twelve": 12, "fifteen": 15, "twenty": 20, "thirty": 30, "forty": 40,
        "fifty": 50, "sixty": 60, "hundred": 100, "a couple of": 2, "a couple": 2}
_NUM_RE = re.compile(r"\b(" + "|".join(sorted(_NUM, key=len, reverse=True)) + r")\s+(?=(?:seconds?|secs?|minutes?|"
                     r"mins?|hours?|hrs?|days?|times?|items?|rows?|users?|screens?|taps?|clicks?|requests?|MB|GB)\b)",
                     re.I)


def normalize(text):
    """Return (text, changes) where changes = [{"kind", "from", "to"}]."""
    changes = []

    def drop(kind):
        def _r(m):
            if m.group(0).strip():
                changes.append({"kind": kind, "from": m.group(0).strip(" ,.!;"), "to": ""})
            return " "
        return _r

    text = re.sub(r"\bwtf\b(?=\s+(?:is|are|does|do|did|happened|happens|was)\b)", "what", text, flags=re.I)
    text = _PHRASES.sub(drop("profanity"), text)
    text = _MASKED.sub(drop("profanity"), text)
    text = _PROFANITY.sub(drop("profanity"), text)
    text = _VENTING.sub(drop("emotion"), text)
    text = _INTENSIFIERS.sub(drop("intensifier"), text)

    def slang(m):
        word = m.group(1)
        to = SLANG[word.lower()]
        changes.append({"kind": "slang", "from": word, "to": to})
        return to

    text = _SLANG_RE.sub(slang, text)

    def num(m):
        to = str(_NUM[m.group(1).lower()])
        changes.append({"kind": "number", "from": m.group(1), "to": to})
        return to + " "

    text = _NUM_RE.sub(num, text)
    text = _CANON_RE.sub(lambda m: CANONICAL[m.group(1).lower()], text)

    # tidy whitespace / punctuation left behind
    text = re.sub(r"[ \t]{2,}", " ", text)
    text = re.sub(r"\s+([,.!?;:])(?=\s|$)", r"\1", text)
    text = re.sub(r"([,;])\s*([,;.!?])", r"\2", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(^|\n)\s*[,;.]\s*", r"\1", text)
    text = re.sub(r"\b(it|this|that|which)\s+(?=[,.])", r"\1 ", text)
    return text.strip(), changes

"""check() and build(): the two operations the CLI and UI call. Input is ONLY your prompt.

  normalize  -> swearing, venting, slang, number words
  cleanup    -> greetings, "could you please", filler
  understand -> objectives, platform, concerns, facts, knowledge-pack questions      (deterministic)
  analyze    -> evidence-based findings + 4 dimension scores + highlight spans       (deterministic)
  local LLM  -> interpretation, extra assumptions/questions; acceptance criteria,
                steps and scope for code changes; rewrites of non-template objectives  (optional)
  spec       -> the final prompt with dynamic blocks and rules
"""

import json
import os
import re
import time

from . import lint, spec
from .cleanup import clean_text, estimate_tokens, protect_materials
from .config import load_config
from .knowledge import CONCERN_BY_ID, platform_pack
from .llm import LLMError, OllamaLLM
from .normalize import normalize
from .understand import CODE_CHANGE, understand

APP_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

ANALYZE_SYSTEM = """You are the AI assistant that will receive the request below. You know nothing about the
user's project except what the request says. A checker has already extracted the objectives, facts and the
standard missing details (listed below). Your job is to find what it could NOT see.

- interpretation: 1-2 sentences: what you would actually produce if you got this request as-is.
- assumptions: up to 4 concrete things you would silently assume that are NOT already covered by the
  ALREADY ASKED list (e.g. where data comes from, which screen, concurrency model, persistence).
- conflicts: statements that contradict each other. Empty if none.
- questions: up to 2 NEW questions not in ALREADY ASKED, only if a wrong guess gives a wrong answer.
  Short, with 2-4 options.
Return only JSON."""

ANALYZE_SCHEMA = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "interpretation": {"type": "string"},
        "assumptions": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
        "conflicts": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
        "questions": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object", "properties": {
            "question": {"type": "string"}, "options": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}},
            "required": ["question"]}},
    },
    "required": ["interpretation", "assumptions"],
}

BUILD_SYSTEM = """You turn a developer's request into precise specification fields for a coding AI.
Rules:
- Use ONLY information in the request, facts and answers. Never invent names, files, versions or requirements.
- objectives: rewrite each listed objective as one precise, imperative sentence, same order, same count.
  Keep the meaning; remove vagueness only with information that was given.
- requirements: concrete must-haves that were stated.
- acceptance_criteria: the stated expected behavior as testable checks ("Given ..., when ..., then ...").
- steps: 3-7 ordered implementation steps using only names from the request. Empty if unclear.
- scope_in / scope_out: what may change / must not change, only if stated.
- open_points: anything still unclear.
Return only JSON."""

BUILD_SCHEMA = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {k: {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}} for k in
                   ("objectives", "requirements", "acceptance_criteria", "steps", "scope_in", "scope_out",
                    "constraints", "open_points")},
    "required": ["objectives"],
}


class Engine:
    def __init__(self, llm_factory=None):
        self.llm_factory = llm_factory or (lambda cfg, model: OllamaLLM(cfg, model))

    # ---------- deterministic stage ----------
    def _prepare(self, req):
        cfg = load_config()
        raw = req.get("prompt") or ""
        protected, materials = protect_materials(raw)
        normalized, changes = normalize(protected)
        clean = clean_text(normalized)
        pack_answers, free_answers = {}, []
        for a in req.get("answers") or []:
            ans = (a.get("answer") or "").strip()
            if not ans:
                continue
            if a.get("id"):
                pack_answers[a["id"]] = ans
            else:
                free_answers.append((a.get("question", "").rstrip("?"), ans))
        und = understand(clean, materials, pack_answers)
        target = req.get("target") or cfg["target"]
        return {"cfg": cfg, "raw": raw, "clean": clean, "materials": materials, "changes": changes, "und": und,
                "target": target, "free_answers": free_answers}

    def _llm(self, cfg, req):
        return self.llm_factory(cfg, req.get("model") or cfg["model"])

    @staticmethod
    def _llm_view(st):
        u = st["und"]
        parts = ["OBJECTIVES:\n" + "\n".join(f"{o['id']}. [{o['label']}] {o['text']}" for o in u["objectives"])]
        if u["facts"]:
            parts.append("FACTS:\n" + "\n".join(f"- {f}" for f in u["facts"]))
        if st["free_answers"]:
            parts.append("ANSWERS:\n" + "\n".join(f"- {q}: {a}" for q, a in st["free_answers"]))
        for i, m in enumerate(st["materials"], 1):
            parts.append(f"PASTED MATERIAL {i}:\n{m[:2500]}")
        return "\n\n".join(parts)

    @staticmethod
    def _understanding_view(u):
        return {
            "platform": platform_pack(u["platform"])["label"],
            "stack": [s["name"] + (f" {s['version']}" if s["version"] else "") for s in u["signals"]["stack"]
                      if s["version"] or s["name"].lower() != platform_pack(u["platform"])["label"].lower()],
            "concerns": [CONCERN_BY_ID[c]["label"] for c in u["signals"]["concerns"]],
            "objectives": [{k: o.get(k) for k in ("id", "intent", "label", "text", "source", "cues", "confidence",
                                                  "templated")} | {"concerns": [CONCERN_BY_ID[c]["label"]
                                                                                for c in o["concerns"]]}
                           for o in u["objectives"]],
            "facts": u["facts"],
            "clues": u["clues"],
            "questions": [{k: q.get(k) for k in ("id", "label", "q", "options", "why", "default", "objective")}
                          for q in u["questions"]],
            "coding": u["coding"],
        }

    # ---------- check ----------
    def check(self, req):
        st = self._prepare(req)
        u = st["und"]
        analysis = lint.analyze(st["raw"], st["clean"], st["materials"], u, st["changes"], st["target"])
        ai = {"interpretation": "", "assumptions": [], "conflicts": [], "questions": []}
        warning = ""
        if not req.get("fast"):
            asked = "\n".join(f"- {q['q']}" for q in u["questions"]) or "- (none)"
            user = self._llm_view(st) + f"\n\nALREADY ASKED:\n{asked}\n\nREQUEST:\n{st['clean']}"
            try:
                data = self._llm(st["cfg"], req).json(ANALYZE_SYSTEM, user, ANALYZE_SCHEMA)
                known = " ".join(q["q"].lower() for q in u["questions"])
                qs = []
                for q in data["questions"][:2]:
                    q = q if isinstance(q, dict) else {"question": q}
                    text = str(q.get("question", "")).strip()
                    key = set(re.findall(r"[a-z]{4,}", text.lower()))
                    if text and len(key & set(re.findall(r"[a-z]{4,}", known))) < max(2, len(key) // 2):
                        qs.append({"question": text, "options": [str(o) for o in q.get("options") or []][:4]})
                ai = {"interpretation": data["interpretation"], "assumptions": data["assumptions"][:4],
                      "conflicts": data["conflicts"][:3], "questions": qs}
            except LLMError as e:
                warning = f"Local model unavailable ({e}). Everything else below still works."
        return {
            "cleaned": st["clean"], "changes": st["changes"], "materials": len(st["materials"]),
            "understanding": self._understanding_view(u),
            "analysis": analysis, "spans": lint.spans(st["raw"], analysis["findings"], st["changes"]),
            "ai": ai, "warning": warning,
        }

    # ---------- build ----------
    def build(self, req):
        started = time.time()
        st = self._prepare(req)
        u = st["und"]
        facts, rejected, _ = spec.split_assumptions(req.get("assumptions"))
        code_change = any(o["intent"] in CODE_CHANGE for o in u["objectives"])
        needs_llm = code_change or any(not o["templated"] for o in u["objectives"])

        fields, warning, model_used = {}, "", "rules only"
        if needs_llm and not req.get("fast"):
            user = self._llm_view(st)
            if facts:
                user += "\n\nCONFIRMED FACTS:\n" + "\n".join(f"- {f}" for f in facts)
            if rejected:
                user += "\n\nREJECTED ASSUMPTIONS:\n" + "\n".join(f"- {r}" for r in rejected)
            user += f"\n\nREQUEST:\n{st['clean']}"
            try:
                llm = self._llm(st["cfg"], req)
                fields = llm.json(BUILD_SYSTEM, user, BUILD_SCHEMA)
                model_used = llm.model
                # keep domain-template objectives; take the model's rewrite only for generic ones
                if len(fields.get("objectives") or []) == len(u["objectives"]):
                    fields["objectives"] = [o["text"] if o["templated"] else (t or o["text"])
                                            for o, t in zip(u["objectives"], fields["objectives"])]
                else:
                    fields.pop("objectives", None)
            except LLMError as e:
                warning = f"Local model step skipped ({e}). Built by the rule-based compiler."
                fields = {}

        prompt, sections, explain = spec.build_spec(
            u, target=st["target"], cfg=st["cfg"], materials=st["materials"], text=st["clean"], fields=fields,
            answers_free=st["free_answers"], assumptions=req.get("assumptions"), conflicts=req.get("conflicts"),
            code_output=req.get("code_output") or st["cfg"]["code_output"],
            efficient=req.get("efficient", st["cfg"]["efficient"]))
        result = {
            "prompt": prompt, "target": st["target"], "warning": warning, "sections": sections, "explain": explain,
            "objectives": len(u["objectives"]),
            "stats": {"input_tokens": estimate_tokens(st["raw"]), "prompt_tokens": estimate_tokens(prompt),
                      "seconds": round(time.time() - started, 1), "model": model_used},
        }
        if st["cfg"].get("save_prompts", True) and not req.get("no_save"):
            result["saved_to"] = self._save(st, result, req)
        return result

    @staticmethod
    def _save(st, result, req):
        base = os.path.join(APP_DIR, "data")
        folder = os.path.join(base, "prompts")
        try:
            os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
            slug = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", st["clean"].lower())[:40].strip("-") or "prompt"
            path = os.path.join(folder, time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S-") + slug + ".md")
            with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(result["prompt"] + "\n")
            with open(os.path.join(base, "history.jsonl"), "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(json.dumps({"time": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "request": st["raw"],
                                    "answers": req.get("answers") or [], "assumptions": req.get("assumptions") or [],
                                    "stats": result["stats"], "file": path}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
            return path
        except OSError:
            return ""
rules.py:
"""Rules: only what THIS prompt needs, each with the reason it was added.

A rule enters the prompt only if something in the request triggers it:
  grounding   - the answer must refer to code that isn't included / target is Claude Code / code was pasted
  version     - a version-sensitive framework is involved and no version was given (framework-specific text)
  concern     - a domain concern was detected (quotes the words that triggered it)
  language    - idioms and pitfalls of the language the answer will be written in, filtered by concern
  team        - your .promptrefiner.json
  scope/accept- only when those blocks exist

Every rule is {"text", "because", "kind"}; the UI shows "because" next to each rule.
There are no always-on rules.
"""

import re

from .knowledge import CONCERN_BY_ID, fill
from .languages import CODE_INTENTS, LANGUAGES, VERSIONED, detect_languages
from .understand import STACK_TERMS

_TECH = {t.lower() for t in STACK_TERMS} | {"fastapi", "testng", "typescript", "javascript", "swiftui", "uikit",
                                            "nextjs", "graphql", "github", "voiceover", "talkback", "webdriver",
                                            "postgresql", "mysql", "mongodb", "nodejs", "springboot", "xcode",
                                            "recyclerview", "lazyvstack", "lazycolumn", "pageobject", "devtools"}

REFERENCE = re.compile(r"\b(my|our|the existing|existing|current|this|that)\s+(?:[\w-]+\s+){0,2}?"
                       r"(function|method|class|file|script|code|component|screen|view ?controller|view model|page|"
                       r"module|service|controller|repository|fragment|activity|adapter|app|project|api|endpoint|"
                       r"page objects?|locators?|list|table)\b", re.I)
CODE_NAME = re.compile(r"\b[a-z]+[A-Z]\w*\b|\b[A-Z][a-z0-9]+[A-Z]\w*\b|\b\w+\(\)|\b[\w-]+\.(?:py|java|kt|ts|tsx|js|"
                       r"jsx|swift|dart|go|rs|cs|php|rb|cpp|sql)\b")


def _rule(text, because, kind):
    return {"text": text, "because": because, "kind": kind}


def produces_code(und):
    return und["coding"] and any(o["intent"] in CODE_INTENTS for o in und["objectives"])


def build_rules(und, *, text, target, has_material, cfg, fields, materials_text=""):
    rules = []
    intents = {o["intent"] for o in und["objectives"]}
    concerns = []
    for o in und["objectives"]:
        concerns += [c for c in o["concerns"] if c not in concerns]
    code = produces_code(und)
    ev = und["signals"]["evidence"]

    # ---------- grounding ----------
    if und["coding"]:
        names = sorted({m.group(0) for m in CODE_NAME.finditer(text)
                        if m.group(0).lower().replace(".", "").replace("()", "") not in _TECH})
        refs = sorted({m.group(0) for m in REFERENCE.finditer(text)})
        if target == "claude-code" and (code or refs or names):
            rules.append(_rule("Open and read the files involved before proposing a change; use the real names from "
                               "the codebase and search before concluding something doesn't exist.",
                               "target is Claude Code", "grounding"))
        elif has_material:
            rules.append(_rule("Refer only to names that appear in <user_material> or this prompt; don't invent other "
                               "classes, functions or APIs of the user's code.", "you pasted code", "grounding"))
        elif code and (names or refs or intents & {"diagnose", "fix", "refactor"}):
            what = (f"you mention {', '.join(repr(x) for x in (names or refs)[:2])} but no code is included"
                    if (names or refs) else "the fix must fit your code, which isn't included")
            rules.append(_rule("You haven't seen the user's code. Don't invent their class, function or file names; "
                               "use clearly marked placeholders (e.g. <YourListViewModel>) and say what to replace.",
                               what, "grounding"))

    # ---------- version traps (specific, not generic) ----------
    if code:
        for v in VERSIONED:
            m = v["_re"].search(text)
            hit = m.group(0) if m else (und["platform"] if v.get("platform") == und["platform"] else "")
            if hit and not v["_ok"].search(text) and not any(r["kind"] == "version" and v.get("platform") and
                                                              v.get("platform") == und["platform"] for r in rules):
                rules.append(_rule(v["text"], f"'{hit}' without a version", "version"))

    # ---------- languages ----------
    langs = detect_languages(text + "\n" + materials_text, und["platform"]) if code else []
    covered = set()
    for lid, evidence, explicit in langs:
        lang = LANGUAGES[lid]
        source = f"'{evidence}'" if explicit else f"{lang['label']} is the default for {evidence}"
        for r in lang["rules"]:
            w = r["when"]
            hit_c = [c for c in w.get("concerns", []) if c in concerns]
            if w.get("concerns") and not hit_c:
                continue
            if w.get("intents") and not intents & set(w["intents"]):
                continue
            covered |= set(hit_c) & {"hang", "concurrency"}       # only generic threading rules are replaced
            why = source
            if hit_c:
                why += " + " + ", ".join(f"'{ev.get(c, c)}'" for c in hit_c[:2])
            rules.append(_rule(r["text"], why, "language"))

    # ---------- concerns (skipped when a language rule already covers that concern) ----------
    for c in concerns:
        if c in covered:
            continue
        for r in CONCERN_BY_ID[c]["rules"]:
            r = fill(r, und["platform"], und.get("answers"))
            if not any(x["text"] == r for x in rules):
                rules.append(_rule(r, f"'{ev.get(c, c)}'", "concern"))

    # ---------- team / scope / acceptance ----------
    if und["coding"]:
        for t in cfg.get("team_rules", []):
            rules.append(_rule(t, "team settings", "team"))
        for b in cfg.get("banned", []):
            rules.append(_rule(f"Do not use: {b}", "team settings (banned)", "team"))
    if fields.get("scope_in") or fields.get("scope_out"):
        rules.append(_rule("Stay inside <scope>; keep all other code and behavior unchanged.", "you set a scope",
                           "scope"))
    if fields.get("acceptance_criteria") and intents & {"fix", "build", "tests", "refactor", "migrate"}:
        rules.append(_rule("Meet every item in <acceptance_criteria>; say in one line each how to verify it.",
                           "you stated the expected behavior", "acceptance"))
    return rules, [(lid, LANGUAGES[lid]["label"]) for lid, _, _ in langs]
spec.py:
"""Compile the final prompt. Every block and every rule is included only when the request needs it.

  <role>               platform + concerns  ("senior iOS engineer specializing in memory and algorithms")
  <context>            facts you gave or answered
  <clues>              what the description itself suggests (from symptom combinations)
  <user_material>      what you pasted, verbatim
  <objectives>         each ask, its domain deliverables, and the answer shape for its intent
  <requirements> <acceptance_criteria> <implementation_steps> <scope>   code changes only
  <constraints>        rejected assumptions, extra limits
  <unknowns>           missing details + the default to use for each
  <rules>              triggered rules only (see rules.py)
  <output_format>      sections / code fences / code mode / brevity

Returns the prompt, a token count per block, and an explanation of why each block and rule is there.
"""

from .cleanup import estimate_tokens
from .knowledge import ANSWER_SHAPE, CONCERN_BY_ID, fill, platform_pack
from .rules import build_rules, produces_code
from .understand import CODE_CHANGE

CODE_OUTPUT = {
    "auto": "",
    "full": "For code changes, give complete files; no placeholders like '...' or '// rest unchanged'.",
    "diff": "For code changes, show only the changed functions/blocks, each labeled with its file and enough "
            "surrounding lines to place it.",
}
EFFICIENT = "Be direct: no preamble, no restating the request, no closing summary."


def _lines(items, numbered=False):
    items = [str(x).strip() for x in items or [] if str(x).strip()]
    return "\n".join(f"{i}. {x}" if numbered else f"- {x}" for i, x in enumerate(items, 1))


def _block(tag, body, attrs=""):
    body = (body or "").strip("\n")
    return f"<{tag}{attrs}>\n{body}\n</{tag}>" if body.strip() else ""


def split_assumptions(assumptions):
    facts, rejected, unsure = [], [], []
    for a in assumptions or []:
        text = (a.get("text") or "").strip()
        if text:
            {"correct": facts, "wrong": rejected}.get(a.get("status"), unsure).append(text)
    return facts, rejected, unsure


def build_role(und):
    intents = [o["intent"] for o in und["objectives"]]
    if not und["coding"]:
        return "You are an expert writer and editor." if "write" in intents else ""
    plat = platform_pack(und["platform"])["label"]
    focuses = []
    for o in und["objectives"]:
        for c in o["concerns"]:
            f = CONCERN_BY_ID[c]["focus"]
            if f not in focuses:
                focuses.append(f)
    noun = "QA automation engineer" if "tests" in intents or "test_automation" in sum(
        (o["concerns"] for o in und["objectives"]), []) else "engineer"
    who = f"a senior {plat + ' ' if plat else 'software '}{noun}"
    if focuses:
        who += " specializing in " + (", ".join(focuses[:-1]) + " and " + focuses[-1] if len(focuses) > 1
                                      else focuses[0])
    return f"You are {who}."


def build_spec(und, *, target, cfg, materials, text="", fields=None, answers_free=None, assumptions=None,
               conflicts=None, code_output="auto", efficient=True):
    fields = fields or {}
    facts, rejected, unsure = split_assumptions(assumptions)
    objectives = und["objectives"]
    texts = fields.get("objectives") if len(fields.get("objectives") or []) == len(objectives) else None
    code_change = any(o["intent"] in CODE_CHANGE for o in objectives)
    code = produces_code(und)
    blocks, explain = [], []

    def add(name, body, why, rules=None):
        if body:
            blocks.append((name, body))
            explain.append({"block": name, "why": why, "rules": rules or [], "tokens": estimate_tokens(body)})

    role = build_role(und)
    add("role", f"<role>{role}</role>" if role else "",
        "Sets the expertise Claude answers from, built from the platform and concerns it detected.")
    ctx = list(und["facts"]) + [f"{q}: {a}" for q, a in (answers_free or [])] + facts
    add("context", _block("context", _lines(ctx)), "Facts you stated or answered, in one place.")
    add("clues", _block("clues", _lines(c["text"] for c in und.get("clues", [])) +
                        ("\nTreat these as hypotheses to verify, not conclusions." if und.get("clues") else "")),
        "What your description already suggests: inferred from symptom combinations, each quoting your words.",
        [{"text": c["text"], "because": f"'{c['evidence']}'" if c["evidence"] else ""} for c in und.get("clues", [])])
    for i, m in enumerate(materials, 1):
        add(f"user_material {i}", _block("user_material", m, f' id="{i}"'), "What you pasted, kept verbatim.")

    # ---- objectives: text + deliverables + answer shape ----
    used, rows = set(), []
    for idx, o in enumerate(objectives):
        t = (texts[idx] if texts and texts[idx] else o["text"]).strip()
        sub = list(o["notes"])
        for c in o["concerns"]:
            if c not in used:
                used.add(c)
                sub += [fill(d, und["platform"], und.get("answers")) for d in CONCERN_BY_ID[c]["deliverables"]]
        shape = ANSWER_SHAPE.get(o["intent"], "")
        if shape:
            sub.append("Answer as: " + shape)
        rows.append(f"{o['id']}. {t}" + "".join(f"\n   - {x}" for x in sub))
    add("objectives", _block("objectives", "\n".join(rows)),
        "Each thing you asked, rewritten as a precise instruction, with what a complete answer must cover and "
        "the structure a senior engineer's answer would have for that kind of ask.")

    if code_change:
        add("requirements", _block("requirements", _lines(fields.get("requirements"))), "Stated must-haves.")
        add("acceptance_criteria", _block("acceptance_criteria", _lines(fields.get("acceptance_criteria"))),
            "Your expected behavior as testable checks.")
        add("implementation_steps", _block("implementation_steps", _lines(fields.get("steps"), numbered=True)),
            "A plan using only names from your prompt.")
    scope = []
    if fields.get("scope_in"):
        scope.append("May change: " + "; ".join(fields["scope_in"]))
    if fields.get("scope_out"):
        scope.append("Must NOT change: " + "; ".join(fields["scope_out"]))
    add("scope", _block("scope", "\n".join(scope)), "What may and may not change.")
    cons = list(fields.get("constraints") or []) + [f"Do not assume: {r}" for r in rejected]
    add("constraints", _block("constraints", _lines(cons)), "Limits, and the assumptions you marked as wrong.")

    # ---- unknowns with defaults ----
    rows = []
    for q in und["open_questions"]:
        rows.append(q["q"] + (f" → if unknown: {q['default']}" if q.get("default") else ""))
    rows += [f"Unconfirmed: {u}" for u in unsure]
    rows += [f"Possible conflict: {c}" for c in conflicts or []]
    rows += fields.get("open_points") or []
    if rows:
        no_default = any(not q.get("default") for q in und["open_questions"])
        if code_change and no_default:
            policy = "If an unknown without a default would change the code, ask about it and stop. Otherwise use the default and say so in one line."
        else:
            policy = "Don't stop to ask: use the default, say so in one line, and note what would change if the real answer differs."
        add("unknowns", _block("unknowns", _lines(rows) + "\n" + policy),
            "Details you didn't give, each with the default Claude should use, so it neither stalls nor guesses "
            "silently.")

    # ---- rules (triggered only) ----
    rules, langs = build_rules(und, text=text, target=target, has_material=bool(materials), cfg=cfg, fields=fields,
                               materials_text="\n".join(materials))
    add("rules", _block("rules", _lines(r["text"] for r in rules)),
        "Only rules something in your prompt triggered. None are always-on.", rules)

    # ---- output format ----
    fmt = []
    if len(objectives) > 1:
        fmt.append("One section per objective, in order, titled '<number>. <3-6 word title>'; don't merge or skip any.")
    if code:
        lang = langs[0][1] if langs else ""
        fmt.append(f"Code in fenced ```{lang.lower().replace('#', 'sharp').replace('++', 'pp')} blocks." if lang
                   else "Code in fenced blocks with the language tag.")
        if code_change and CODE_OUTPUT.get(code_output):
            fmt.append(CODE_OUTPUT[code_output])
    if efficient:
        fmt.append(EFFICIENT)
    add("output_format", _block("output_format", _lines(fmt)), "How the answer should be laid out.")

    prompt = "\n\n".join(b for _, b in blocks)
    return prompt, [(n, estimate_tokens(b)) for n, b in blocks], explain
understand.py:
"""Understand a prompt the way a senior engineer would before answering it.

  extract_signals()  platform, stated stack + versions, concerns, timings, data sizes
  segment()          split a multi-part message into separate asks
  classify()         intent of each ask: diagnose · fix · advise · explain · build · tests · refactor ·
                     migrate · review · write
  understand()       -> objectives (each rewritten as a precise instruction), context facts,
                        open questions with options, and the evidence that triggered everything

Deterministic: no model needed. The local model only adds to it.
"""

import re

from .knowledge import CONCERN_BY_ID, CONCERNS, PLATFORMS, default_for, fill, find_clues, platform_pack

# ==========================================================================
# Intents
# ==========================================================================
INTENTS = {
    "diagnose": {"label": "Diagnose & fix", "code": True},
    "fix": {"label": "Fix a bug", "code": True},
    "advise": {"label": "Recommend", "code": False},
    "explain": {"label": "Explain", "code": False},
    "build": {"label": "Build", "code": True},
    "tests": {"label": "Write tests", "code": True},
    "refactor": {"label": "Refactor", "code": True},
    "migrate": {"label": "Migrate", "code": True},
    "review": {"label": "Review", "code": False},

CODE_CHANGE = {"fix", "build", "tests", "refactor", "migrate"}

_SYMPTOM = re.compile(r"\b(hangs?|hanging|freez\w*|frozen|unresponsive|not responding|leak\w*|crash\w*|lag\w*|"

                      r"flaky|timeouts?|times? out|stuck)\b", re.I)
_SOLVE = re.compile(r"\b(fix|solve|solution|avoid|prevent|stop|get rid of|reduce|debug|why)\b", re.I)
_QUESTION_START = re.compile(r"^\s*(what|which|how|why|when|where|who|should|could|can|would|will|is|are|do|does|did)\b",
                             re.I)
_ADVISE = re.compile(r"\b(best|better|good|right|ideal|recommend\w*|suggest\w*|should i|should we|which one|"

                      r"walk me through|difference between|understand|meaning of)\b", re.I)
_FIX = re.compile(r"\b(fix|bug|error|exception|broken|not working|doesn'?t work|isn'?t working|wrong (?:output|result|"
                  r"value)|regression|fails?|failing)\b", re.I)
_TESTS = re.compile(r"\b(write|create|add|automate|generate)\b.{0,40}\b(tests?|test cases?|automation|scripts?)\b|"
                    r"\b(selenium|appium|playwright|cypress|espresso|xcuitest)\b", re.I)
_REFACTOR = re.compile(r"\b(refactor\w*|clean ?up|restructure|simplify|extract|rename|reorgani[sz]e|decouple)\b", re.I)
_MIGRATE = re.compile(r"\b(migrat\w*|upgrad\w*|port(?:ing)? (?:to|from)|convert\w* .{0,30}\bto\b|move from)\b", re.I)
_REVIEW = re.compile(r"\b(review|audit|look over|feedback on)\b", re.I)
_BUILD = re.compile(r"\b(add|implement|create|build|make|develop|generate|write|set up|setup|integrate)\b", re.I)
_WRITE = re.compile(r"\b(blog|post|email|essay|article|caption|script|story|letter|summary|summari[sz]e|tweet|"
                    r"thread|newsletter|description|bio|report|speech|poem)\b", re.I)
_CODEY_WORDS = re.compile(r"\b(code|app|function|method|class|api|bug|screen|ui|list|database|query|component|"
                          r"server|module|library|algorithm|test|endpoint|view|layout|button|feature)\b", re.I)
_CODEY_NAMES = re.compile(r"\b[a-z]+[A-Z]\w*\b|\w+\(\)|\b\w+\.(?:py|java|kt|swift|ts|js|dart)\b")


_INTENT_CUES = {
    "diagnose": ["_SYMPTOM", "_SOLVE"], "advise": ["_QUESTION_START", "_ADVISE"], "explain": ["_EXPLAIN"],
    "fix": ["_FIX"], "tests": ["_TESTS"], "refactor": ["_REFACTOR"], "migrate": ["_MIGRATE"], "review": ["_REVIEW"],
    "build": ["_BUILD", "_HOW_BUILD"], "write": ["_WRITE", "_BUILD"],
}


def intent_cues(seg, intent):
    """The words that made us choose this intent, and a confidence level."""
    cues = []
    for name in _INTENT_CUES.get(intent, []):
        for m in globals()[name].finditer(seg):
            w = m.group(0).strip()
            if w and w.lower() not in [c.lower() for c in cues]:
                cues.append(w)
    conf = "high" if len(cues) >= 2 else "medium" if cues else "low"
    return cues[:5], conf


def _codey(s):
    return bool(_CODEY_WORDS.search(s) or _CODEY_NAMES.search(s))


_HOW_BUILD = re.compile(r"^how (?:do|can|should|would) (?:i|we|you) (?:add|implement|create|make|build|set up|setup|"
                        r"integrate|write|generate)\b", re.I)


def classify(seg):
    """Intent of one ask."""
    s = seg.strip()
    is_q = bool(_QUESTION_START.match(s)) or s.endswith("?")
    if _SYMPTOM.search(s) and (_SOLVE.search(s) or is_q or not _BUILD.search(s)):
        return "diagnose"
    if _TESTS.search(s):
        return "tests"
    if _MIGRATE.search(s):
        return "migrate"
    if _REFACTOR.search(s):
        return "refactor"
    if _REVIEW.search(s):
        return "review"
    if _HOW_BUILD.match(s):
        return "build"
    if is_q and _ADVISE.search(s) and not _EXPLAIN.match(s):
        return "advise"
    if is_q or _EXPLAIN.search(s):
        return "explain" if _EXPLAIN.search(s) or is_q else "general"
    if _FIX.search(s):
        return "fix"
    if _WRITE.search(s) and not _codey(s):
        return "write"
    if _BUILD.search(s):
        return "build" if _codey(s) else "write"
    return "general"

               "Flutter", "Dart", "React Native", "React", "Vue", "Angular", "Next.js", "TypeScript", "JavaScript",

               "Cypress", "TestNG", "JUnit", "pytest", "Espresso", "XCUITest", "Combine", "RxSwift", "Alamofire",
               "Retrofit", "GraphQL", "Docker", "Kubernetes", "AWS", "MT5", "MQL5", "Pandas", "TensorFlow", "PyTorch"]
_STACK_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.#+])(" + "|".join(re.escape(t) for t in sorted(STACK_TERMS, key=len, reverse=True))
                       + r")(?![\w#+])(?:\s*(?:v|version\s*)?(\d+(?:\.\d+){0,2}))?", re.I)
_TIME_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:after|within|in|for)\s+(?:about\s+|around\s+|roughly\s+|~\s*)?(\d+|a few|few|several)\s*"
                      r"(seconds?|secs?|minutes?|mins?|hours?|hrs?)(?:\s+of)?(?:\s+(usage|use|using it|scrolling|"
                      r"running|idle))?", re.I)
_SIZE_RE = re.compile(r"\b(\d[\d,.]*\s*(?:k|K|m|M|thousand|million|lakh)?)\s*(items?|rows?|records?|elements?|entries|"
                      r"products?|users?|objects?|cells?)\b", re.I)
_VAGUE_SIZE_RE = re.compile(r"\b(large|huge|big|long|massive|lots of|a lot of|many|thousands of|millions of)\s+"
                            r"(?:\w+\s+)?(list\w*|data\w*|arrays?|tables?|items?|records?|rows?|collections?)\b", re.I)
_DATA_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:the |a |my |our )?(list|array|table|collection|feed|dataset)\b(?:\s+of\s+(\w+))?",
                      re.I)


def extract_signals(text, materials=()):
    blob = text + "\n" + "\n".join(materials)
    platforms, evidence = [], {}
    for pid, pack in PLATFORMS.items():
        m = pack["_re"].search(blob)
        if m:
            platforms.append(pid)
            evidence[pid] = m.group(0)
    if "react-native" in platforms and "web" in platforms:
        platforms.remove("web")
    stack, seen = [], set()
    for m in _STACK_RE.finditer(text):
        name = next(t for t in STACK_TERMS if t.lower() == m.group(1).lower())
        if name.lower() not in seen:
            seen.add(name.lower())
            stack.append({"name": name, "version": m.group(2) or ""})
        elif m.group(2):
            for s in stack:
                if s["name"].lower() == name.lower() and not s["version"]:
                    s["version"] = m.group(2)
    concerns = []
    for c in CONCERNS:
        m = c["_re"].search(text)
        if m:
            concerns.append(c["id"])
            evidence[c["id"]] = m.group(0)
    t = _TIME_RE.search(text)
    timing = ""
    if t:
        n, unit = t.group(1), t.group(2).lower()
        unit = {"secs": "seconds", "sec": "seconds", "mins": "minutes", "min": "minutes", "hrs": "hours",
                "hr": "hours"}.get(unit, unit)
        if n.isdigit() and int(n) == 1:
            unit = unit.rstrip("s")
        doing = t.group(3) or "use"
        doing = {"usage": "use", "using it": "use"}.get(doing.lower(), doing.lower())
        timing = f"after about {n} {unit} of {doing}"
        evidence["timing"] = t.group(0)
    sizes = [f"{m.group(1).strip()} {m.group(2)}" for m in _SIZE_RE.finditer(text)]
    vague = _VAGUE_SIZE_RE.search(text)
    if vague:
        evidence["vague_size"] = vague.group(0)
    d = _DATA_RE.search(text)
    data = ""
    if d:
        data = f"the {d.group(1).lower()}" + (f" of {d.group(2)}" if d.group(2) else "")
    return {"platforms": platforms, "stack": stack, "concerns": concerns, "timing": timing, "sizes": sizes,
            "vague_size": bool(vague) and not sizes, "data": data, "evidence": evidence}

_SPLIT_INSIDE = re.compile(
    r"\s*(?:,\s*|;\s*)?\b(?:so|and also|also|and then|plus|additionally|then)\b\s+(?=(?:what|which|how|why|should|"
    r"could|can|is|are|do|does|please|i also|add|fix|make|create|write|implement|explain|tell)\b)"
    r"|,\s*(?=(?:what|which|how|why|and how|and what)\b)", re.I)


def segment(text):
    parts = []
    for line in re.split(r"\n+", text):
        line = re.sub(r"^\s*(?:[-*•]|\d+[.)])\s+", "", line).strip()
        if not line or re.fullmatch(r"\[MATERIAL \d+\]", line):
            continue
        for sent in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+(?=[A-Z\[])", line):
            for piece in _SPLIT_INSIDE.split(sent):
                piece = piece.strip(" ,;")
                if len(piece.split()) >= 2:
                    parts.append(piece)
    return parts


def _depersonalize(s):
    s = re.sub(r"\bmy\b", "the", s, flags=re.I)
    s = re.sub(r"\bour\b", "the", s, flags=re.I)
    s = re.sub(r"\b(?:me|us)\b", "the user", s)
    return s


_STATEMENT = re.compile(r"^(?:i|we)\s+(?:have to|need to|must|want to|am trying to|'m trying to|are trying to|"
                        r"am going to|have|use|am using|'m using|are using)\s+(.+)$", re.I)

_Q_RULES = [
    (re.compile(r"^how (?:do|can|should|would) (?:i|we|you) (?P<v>add|implement|create|make|build|set up|setup|"
                r"integrate|write|generate) (?P<rest>.*)$", re.I), "{v} {rest}, and show the code"),
    (re.compile(r"^(?:which|what)(?: one)? (?:is|would be|works) (?:better|best|faster|preferable|more efficient)"
                r"(?: for (?P<for>[^,]+?))?,?\s*(?:between\s+)?(?P<opts>[\w .+#-]+?\s+(?:or|vs\.?|versus)\s+[\w .+#-]+)$",
                re.I), "Compare {opts} for {for} and recommend one"),  # " or " -> " and " applied below
    (re.compile(r"^(?:what|which)\s+(?:kind of\s+|type of\s+|sort of\s+)?(?P<n>[\w\s-]{1,30}?)\s+(?:should|would|will|"
                r"can|could|do|does)\s+(?:i|we|you)\s+(?:use|apply|choose|pick|implement|go with|take|do)\s*"
                r"(?P<rest>.*)$", re.I), "Recommend the best {n} {rest}"),
    (re.compile(r"^(?:what|which)\s+(?:kind of\s+|type of\s+)?(?P<n>[\w\s-]{1,30}?)\s+(?:is|feels?|works?|would be|"
                r"seems?|looks?)\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:best|good|better|right|fastest|ideal|most efficient)\s*(?P<rest>.*)$",
                re.I), "Recommend the best {n} {rest}"),
    (re.compile(r"^how (?:do|can|should|would) (?:i|we|you) (?P<rest>.*)$", re.I), "Explain how to {rest}"),
    (re.compile(r"^why (?:does|is|do|are|did|would|is it that) (?P<rest>.*)$", re.I), "Explain why {rest}"),
    (re.compile(r"^what (?:is|are) (?:the )?(?:difference between )(?P<rest>.*)$", re.I),
     "Explain the difference between {rest}"),
    (re.compile(r"^what (?:is|are|does) (?P<rest>.*)$", re.I), "Explain what {rest}"),
    (re.compile(r"^(?:can|could|would|will) you (?P<rest>.*)$", re.I), "{rest}"),
    (re.compile(r"^(?:should|is it better to) (?:i|we) (?P<rest>.*)$", re.I), "Recommend whether to {rest}"),
]


def question_to_instruction(s):
    s = s.strip().rstrip("?.! ").strip()
    for rx, tpl in _Q_RULES:
        m = rx.match(s)
        if m:
            groups = {k: (v or "").strip() for k, v in m.groupdict().items()}
            if "opts" in groups:
                groups["opts"] = re.sub(r"\s+(?:or|vs\.?|versus)\s+", " and ", groups["opts"])
                if not groups.get("for"):
                    tpl = tpl.replace(" for {for}", "")
            out = tpl.format(**groups)
            out = re.sub(r"\s{2,}", " ", out).strip()
            return out[0].upper() + out[1:] + "."
    return s[0].upper() + s[1:] + ("?" if _QUESTION_START.match(s) else ".")


def _objective_text(seg, intent, sig, gsig):
    """(text, templated) - precise instruction for one ask, using templates where the domain is known."""
    t = _template_text(seg, intent, sig, gsig)
    return (t, True) if t else (question_to_instruction(_depersonalize(seg)), False)


def _template_text(seg, intent, sig, gsig):
    pid = (sig["platforms"] or gsig["platforms"] or [""])[0]
    plat = platform_pack(pid)["label"]
    app = f"the {plat} app" if plat else "the app"
    timing = f" {sig['timing'] or gsig['timing']}" if (sig["timing"] or gsig["timing"]) else ""
    cs = set(sig["concerns"])
    sizes = sig["sizes"] or gsig["sizes"]
    size = f" ({sizes[0]})" if sizes else (" (large; exact size not stated)" if (sig["vague_size"] or
                                                                                gsig["vague_size"]) else "")
    data = sig["data"] or gsig["data"] or "the data"
    if intent == "diagnose":
        if "memory" in cs and "hang" in cs:
            return (f"Find the likely cause(s) of the memory leak that makes {app} become unresponsive{timing}, "
                    "explain how to confirm each one, and give the fix.")
        if "memory" in cs:
            return f"Find the likely cause(s) of the memory leak in {app}{timing}, explain how to confirm each one, and give the fix."
        if "hang" in cs:
            word = (sig["evidence"].get("hang") or "").lower()
            if re.match(r"lag|stutter|jank|slow", word):
                where = " while scrolling" if re.search(r"scroll", seg, re.I) else ""
                return (f"Find why {app} lags{where}{size}{timing}, explain how to confirm the cause, and give "
                        "the fix.")
            return f"Find why {app} becomes unresponsive{timing}, explain how to confirm the cause, and give the fix."
        if "crash" in cs:
            return f"Find the cause of the crash in {app}{timing} and give the fix."
        if "performance" in cs:
            return f"Find why {app} is slow{timing}, show how to measure it, and give the fix."
    if intent == "advise":
        if "sorting" in cs:
            return f"Recommend the best way to sort {data}{size}, including its time and space complexity."
        if "large_list" in cs:
            return f"Recommend how to display {data}{size} efficiently."
    return None


def understand(text, materials=(), answers=None):
    """text: normalized + cleaned prompt (code blocks replaced by [MATERIAL n])."""
    answers = answers or {}
    gsig = extract_signals(text, materials)
    if (answers.get("data_size") or "").strip():
        size = answers["data_size"].strip()
        gsig["sizes"] = [size if re.search(r"[a-z]{3,}", size, re.I) else size + " items"]
        gsig["vague_size"] = False
    objectives, context = [], []
    pending_statements, pending_concerns = [], []
    for seg in segment(text):
        sig = extract_signals(seg)
        leftover = _STACK_RE.sub("", seg)
        if sig["stack"] and len(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z]{3,}", leftover)) < 2:
            continue                                                # e.g. "Python 3.12 FastAPI." -> a fact only
        st = _STATEMENT.match(seg)
        intent = classify(seg)
        if st and not _QUESTION_START.match(seg) and intent in ("general", "build", "write") and not \
                re.search(r"\b(add|implement|create|build|write|make)\b", st.group(1), re.I):
            pending_statements.append(_depersonalize(st.group(1)).rstrip(".") + ".")
            pending_concerns += [c for c in sig["concerns"] if c not in pending_concerns]
            continue
        if intent == "general" and not _QUESTION_START.match(seg) and objectives:
            context.append(_depersonalize(seg).rstrip(".") + ".")      # extra detail for the previous ask
            continue
        sig["concerns"] = pending_concerns + [c for c in sig["concerns"] if c not in pending_concerns]
        if gsig["sizes"]:
            sig["sizes"], sig["vague_size"] = gsig["sizes"], False
        obj_text, templated = _objective_text(seg, intent, sig, gsig)
        cues, conf = intent_cues(seg, intent)
        obj = {"id": len(objectives) + 1, "intent": intent, "label": INTENTS[intent]["label"],
               "cues": cues, "confidence": conf,
               "source": seg, "concerns": sig["concerns"], "text": obj_text, "templated": templated,
               "notes": [f"Requirement: {s}" for s in pending_statements]}
        pending_statements, pending_concerns = [], []
        words = set(re.findall(r"[a-z]{3,}", obj["text"].lower()))
        obj["notes"] = [n for n in obj["notes"]                       # drop notes the objective already says
                        if not set(re.findall(r"[a-z]{3,}", n.lower())) - {"requirement"} <= words]
        objectives.append(obj)
    if not objectives:
        objectives.append({"id": 1, "intent": classify(text), "label": INTENTS[classify(text)]["label"],
                           "cues": intent_cues(text, classify(text))[0], "confidence": intent_cues(text, classify(text))[1],
                           "source": text, "concerns": gsig["concerns"], "text": question_to_instruction(text),
                           "templated": False, "notes": []})
        objectives[0]["label"] = INTENTS[objectives[0]["intent"]]["label"]
    for s in pending_statements:
        context.append("Requirement: " + s)

    # concerns found anywhere but not attached to an objective go to the first matching / first objective
    attached = {c for o in objectives for c in o["concerns"]}
    for c in gsig["concerns"]:
        if c not in attached:
            objectives[0]["concerns"].append(c)

    coding = any(INTENTS[o["intent"]]["code"] for o in objectives) or bool(gsig["platforms"]) or \
        bool(gsig["stack"]) or any(c in gsig["concerns"] for c in ("sorting", "memory", "hang", "crash",
                                                                    "concurrency", "database", "large_list"))
    pid = (gsig["platforms"] or [""])[0]

    # ---- questions a senior engineer would ask, from the knowledge packs ----
    questions, seen = [], set()
    pplat = platform_pack(pid)
    if pplat.get("ui_question") and any(c in gsig["concerns"] for c in ("memory", "hang", "large_list", "performance")) \
            and not re.search(pplat["ui_satisfied"], text, re.I):
        q, opts = pplat["ui_question"]
        questions.append({"id": "ui_framework", "label": "UI framework", "q": q, "options": opts,
                          "why": f"Leak patterns and list rendering differ between {' and '.join(opts[:2])}.",
                          "severity": "warn", "concern": "platform", "evidence": gsig["evidence"].get(pid, ""),
                          "default": default_for("ui_framework", pid), "objective": 0})
        seen.add("ui_framework")
    for o in objectives:
        for cid in o["concerns"]:
            for q in CONCERN_BY_ID[cid]["questions"]:
                if q["id"] in seen or re.search(q["satisfied"], text + "\n" + "\n".join(materials), re.I):
                    continue
                seen.add(q["id"])
                questions.append({"id": q["id"], "label": q["label"], "q": fill(q["q"], pid),
                                  "options": q["options"], "why": q["why"], "severity": q.get("severity", "warn"),
                                  "concern": cid, "evidence": gsig["evidence"].get(cid, ""),
                                  "default": default_for(q["id"], pid), "objective": o["id"]})
    open_questions = [q for q in questions if not (answers.get(q["id"]) or "").strip()]
    answered = [(q["label"], answers[q["id"]].strip()) for q in questions if (answers.get(q["id"]) or "").strip()]

    # ---- facts ----
    facts = []
    if pid:
        facts.append(f"Platform: {platform_pack(pid)['label']}")
    stack_line = ", ".join(s["name"] + (f" {s['version']}" if s["version"] else "") for s in gsig["stack"]
                           if s["name"].lower() != (platform_pack(pid)["label"] or "").lower() or s["version"])
    if stack_line:
        facts.append(f"Stack (as stated): {stack_line}")
    if gsig["timing"] and any(c in gsig["concerns"] for c in ("memory", "hang", "crash", "performance")):
        sym = "becomes unresponsive" if "hang" in gsig["concerns"] else "shows the problem"
        facts.append(f"Symptom: the app {sym} {gsig['timing']}")
    if gsig["sizes"]:
        facts.append("Data size: " + ", ".join(gsig["sizes"]))
    elif gsig["vague_size"]:
        facts.append("Data size: described as large; exact count not stated")
    facts += [f"{label}: {value}" for label, value in answered if label != "Data size"]
    facts += context

    concerns_all = []
    for o in objectives:
        concerns_all += [c for c in o["concerns"] if c not in concerns_all]
    clues = find_clues(text, concerns_all, {o["intent"] for o in objectives}, gsig["timing"],
                       gsig["evidence"].get("timing", ""))
    if answers.get("memory_pattern", "").lower().startswith("keeps rising"):
        clues.insert(0, {"id": "leak_confirmed", "evidence": answers["memory_pattern"],
                         "text": "Memory keeps rising until the hang, so this is a leak or unbounded growth, not just "
                                 "a slow operation; prioritise retained objects over CPU work."})
    elif answers.get("memory_pattern", "").lower().startswith("stays flat"):
        clues.insert(0, {"id": "main_thread", "evidence": answers["memory_pattern"],
                         "text": "Memory stays flat while the UI freezes, so the main thread is blocked (heavy work, a "
                                 "lock or a synchronous call); prioritise CPU/main-thread work over leaks."})
    return {"signals": gsig, "platform": pid, "objectives": objectives, "facts": facts, "coding": coding,
            "questions": questions, "open_questions": open_questions, "answers": answers, "clues": clues}
